thread: Anya Ivanova: Heads-up — saw a regressing tail on paged-attn in canary this morning. p50 looks fine but p99 jumped ~2.5x after the latest kernel selector change. Investigating.
messages: Anya Ivanova: repro steps: run bench_runner with long-seq mix (some requests ~2k tokens). I saw this command: `./bench_runner --model paged-attn-alloc --mix long-short --runs 200` and p99 for a single card went from ~120ms -> ~310ms after deploy.
Raj Patel: ack. which kernel path is being chosen for the long ones? flash variants or paged fused?

Anya Ivanova: looks like we flip between flash_v2 and paged_fused depending on batch composition. The selector uses a heuristic: prefer fused when avg_seq > 512 OR KV hits > 20% but that heuristic seems to thrash when mixed batches appear.
Mike Chen: that kernel flip sounds bad. If batches contain a few long requests, the runtime toggles kernel mid-batch? I thought we pick per-batch not per-request.

Anya Ivanova: we do pick per-batch, but batching heuristic groups by arrival time. So when a long request arrives in an otherwise short batch, the selector computes a different preferred kernel and we end up switching kernels across consecutive batches. The overhead is kernel warmup + different shared workspace sizing -> extra memcpy + kernel init stalls.

Lin Park: could also be KV cache paging churn. If long seqs cause lots of KV page faults, the pager evicts pages and then the next batch needs to fetch back. I saw the pager stats spike in the same window.
Sara Gomez: perf bot traces? perf-bot, can you post the flamegraph or perf summary for the offending run?

perf-bot: Attached summary from 2961234567-run: total tokens=1.2M, avg_batch_size=4.2, kernel_mode_switches=86, kv_page_reads=3200, memcpy_ms=42. Flamegraph link: https://perf.internal/reports/2961234567 (private)

Mike Chen: memcpy_ms=42 is a lot relative to p50. If kernel switches trigger reallocation of pinned buffers and extra memcpy, that'll blow the tail. We need to make kernel selection sticky for N batches or prefer the lower-overhead kernel in ambiguous cases.

Anya Ivanova: quick experiment: I patched selector to prefer 'flash_v2' whenever >30% short requests in a batch, even if avg_seq >512. Ran 1000 samples locally: p50 roughly unchanged, p99 reduced from 310ms -> 165ms. Patch: https://git.internal/r/eng-runtime/p/r/4823
Raj Patel: nice. Does that impact output quality or token throughput for truly long-only workloads?
Anya Ivanova: for long-only (all seq >1500) flash_v2 is marginally slower than paged_fused (~+6%), but much more stable. For mixed workloads, flash_v2 wins tail by large margin.

Lin Park: we should also look at KV pager prefetch heuristics. Right now pager fetches exactly the requested pages. If we prefetch the next 1-2 pages for long requests, we amortize IO. But prefetch can waste memory.
Mike Chen: agree. Another angle: reduce kernel warmup penalty by keeping a small pool of pre-allocated workspace per kernel per-device. That avoids re-malloc on kernel flip. Cost is modest memory.
Sara Gomez: ops question: if we change selector to sticky or bias to flash_v2, do we need a config flag rollout? Can we hotpatch?

Raj Patel: we can gate behind a runtime flag `ATTN_KERNEL_STICKY=1` and rollout via canary. Also add a telemetry metric `kernel_switch_rate` per shard so we can monitor. CI bot should add integration perf test.
ci-bot: created perf test job `paged-attn-selector-mix` and added to nightly matrix. Job id: nightly-296123; see: https://ci.internal/jobs/nightly-296123
Anya Ivanova: added a quick regression dashboard: p50/p95/p99 for paged-attn, plus kernel_switch_rate, kv_page_reads, memcpy_ms. Dash link: https://dash.internal/paged-attn/296123

Mike Chen: quick profiling notes (from perf container):
```
# perf top sample
- paged_kernel_dispatch       18%
- memcpy_h2d                 12%
- kv_page_read_async         9%
- flash_v2_attention         7%
- scheduler_lock             6%
```
This suggests dispatch + memcpy + pager IO are the big parts of tail.

Anya Ivanova: I'm going to run 3 experiments:
1) selector sticky (N=5 batches) + sticky timeout
2) keep flash_v2 as tie-breaker for mixed batches
3) pre-alloc kernel workspaces
I'll run in canary and post numbers.
Raj Patel: add one more: try pager prefetch=2 for long reads (configurable per workload). Also profile kv page allocation: fragmented pages cause extra carve-outs -> more memcpy.

Lin Park: note about allocator: the block table lookups cost is proportional to fragments-per-request. If we group long requests by shard affinity (hot keys), we reduce fragmentation. Might be a future improvement: affinity-aware batching.
Sara Gomez: timeline? we should aim to have sticky selector behind flag this week so we can roll and observe overnight traffic.
Anya Ivanova: agreed. Will open PR with tests + telemetry and add to canary. Planned rollout: flag on -> ramp 1% -> 10% -> 100% if p99 improves.
Mike Chen: make sure to record a small benchmark table in the PR: p50/p95/p99 for configs (baseline, sticky, prealloc, prefetch). That helps product/ops understand tradeoffs.
Anya Ivanova: will do. Early local numbers: baseline p99=310ms, sticky p99=160ms, sticky+prealloc p99=150ms, sticky+prealloc+prefetch p99=135ms. I'll push data to PR.
Raj Patel: excellent. Long-term we should consider a cost model: pick kernel to minimize expected cost = latency_penalty * SLAs + GPU_time * $/ms. That will let us balance throughput vs tail.
Lin Park: and add an internal eval harness that simulates mixed client mixes so we won't regress on these patterns in future.
Anya Ivanova: thanks all. I'll post canary results tomorrow. If anyone wants to help with the prefetch impl or allocator profiling ping me. :party_parrot:
Mike Chen: pinged. Happy to help with allocator traces.

Sara Gomez: closing loop: after Anya's canary runs, we'll decide whether to keep flag and backfill to prod. :eyes:

Anya Ivanova: update 2961234800: canary (3 hosts, ~10k reqs) results: baseline p99=308ms, sticky p99=162ms, sticky+prealloc+prefetch p99=128ms. Rolling to 10% now. Putting numbers into PR and dashboard.
Raj Patel: great. Follow-up tickets: #6123 affinity-aware batching, #6124 pager-prefetch tuning, #6125 kernel-workspace-pool. I'll file them.
Anya Ivanova: filed. Thanks everyone.
